context/same_cote_33/MPL_33_098-146_note.text: “Il semble que pour les courbes, on récupère … (sans résolution des singularités) … $\rightsquigarrow$ rationalité des fonctions $L$” is a proposed application of the formalism, not a proved curve theorem on this page. A proof would have to identify the extension-by-zero or immersion argument, justify the local terms for the singular coefficient sheaf, and then pass from the trace identities to the Euler product/determinant identity. The finished SGA 5 provides distinct comparison destinations for Lefschetz and for rationality, but the present evidence does not identify this draft with a particular circulated version (Grothendieck, 1977, Exposé III; Illusie, 1977, volume contents).

context/same_cote_33/MPL_33_098-146_note.section: ### N38. The deleted boundedness condition has mathematical consequences
context/same_cote_33/MPL_33_098-146_note.text: In the inserted phrase “loc. libre de t.f., et borné,” the words “et borné” are themselves deleted, so they cannot be treated as a surviving hypothesis on this page. An infinite direct sum of contractible two-term free complexes placed in disjoint, successively negative degrees represents the zero, hence perfect, derived object, yet its identity has no finite degreewise alternating sum on that unbounded representative. Thus the literal representative-based formula needs local bounded representatives or another specified interpretation; this is a conditional scope objection, not a reason to restore the deletion or deny the intrinsic trace of the perfect object.

context/same_cote_33/MPL_33_098-146_note.section: ### N54. The literal étale criterion admits a dual-number counterexample
context/same_cote_33/MPL_33_098-146_note.text: In condition (c), finite separability of $\kappa(y)/\kappa(x)$ alone does not imply the subsequent equality $m_y=m_xO_y$: $\operatorname{Spec}(k[\varepsilon]/\varepsilon^2)\to\operatorname{Spec}k$ is finite, flat and finitely presented, with residue extension $k/k$, but has $m_y=(\varepsilon)\ne0$. Its nonreduced fibre prevents étaleness, in agreement with the criterion requiring étale fibres (The Stacks Project Authors, n.d., [Tag 03PC](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/03PC), Proposition 59.26.2). This is a counterexample to the isolated residue-field-only wording as transcribed, not to the stronger condition printed immediately afterward or to an unseen theorem elsewhere.

context/same_cote_33/MPL_33_098-146_note.section: ### N08. Finite coefficient rings force attention to unbounded resolutions
context/same_cote_33/MPL_33_098-146_note.text: The warning that $\mathbb Z/n\mathbb Z$ is not a field and need not have finite global Tor dimension explains the move from degree-zero sheaves into $D^-$, while 112 emphasizes that tensor and derived Hom can have unbounded cohomological effects even at a geometric point. The opening remark on 108 explicitly leaves finite-Tor and finite-Ext refinements outside the current scope. This is a methodological precursor to the perfect-complex trace construction on 130–146, not evidence that all finite coefficient modules are perfect. The literal warning about $\mathbb Z/n\mathbb Z$ also needs arithmetic scope: squarefree $n$ gives a product of fields, whereas $n=\ell^2$ gives the actual obstruction checked in N10.

context/same_cote_33/MPL_33_098-146_note.section: ### N09. The noetherian expectation for relative direct image
context/same_cote_33/MPL_33_098-146_note.text: “C'est peut-être vrai dès que $Y$ est noethérien” concerns finite **relative** cohomological dimension of $f_*$, in the surrounding finite-type discussion, rather than finite absolute cohomological dimension of $Y$. The finite-type-over-a-field case has a direct modern counterpart (The Stacks Project Authors, n.d., [Tag 0F10](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/0F10)), and Illusie (2014, Exposé XVIII_A, Corollary 1.4) proves the relative $\ell$-torsion statement for finite-dimensional noetherian $Y$ with $\ell$ invertible on $Y$. Those results confirm qualified versions; these notes leave the draft's full “merely noetherian” scope unresolved and do not offer the absolute cohomology of a field as a counterexample to it.

The Stacks Project Authors (n.d., [Tag 0F14](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/0F14), Lemma 59.97.2(2)) confirms this one-proper-factor formula for finite-type schemes over a separably closed field and arbitrary $\mathbb Z/n\mathbb Z$ complexes, without assuming $n$ invertible. This comparison supports the manuscript's distinction rather than transferring the later prime-to-characteristic condition backwards to all Künneth formulas in the package.

context/same_cote_33/MPL_33_098-146_note.section: ### N16. An explicit characteristic-p failure in degree one
context/same_cote_33/MPL_33_098-146_note.text: For algebraically closed $k$ of characteristic $p$, Artin–Schreier gives $H^1_{\mathrm{ét}}(\mathbb A_k^2,\mathbb F_p)=k[x,y]/\{h^p-h\}$ (The Stacks Project Authors, n.d., [Tag 0A3J](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/0A3J)). The class of $xy$ does not come from the sum of the two one-variable cohomology groups: an equality $xy=a(x)+b(y)+h^p-h$ would leave, after discarding pure-variable monomials, a mixed polynomial $q$ with $q^p-q=xy$, which is impossible by its highest total degree. This checks the manuscript's failure claim and is consistent with the doubtful addition “même pour $H^1$,” but it gives no permission to remove that paleographic doubt from the frozen text.

The later exposition and its publication history are comparison material, not a basis for upgrading “aurait” to a verified priority claim.

context/same_cote_33/MPL_33_098-146_note.text: The manuscript uses one fixed interval for “tout pt géom,” a quantifier that should be retained in any reconstruction. On a disjoint union of infinitely many points, put a copy of $A$ in cohomological degree $-n$ on the $n$th component: this is locally perfect and bounded above, with finite Tor-amplitude at every stalk, but it has no single global finite amplitude interval. The example distinguishes the manuscript's uniform claim from the local perfectness criterion (The Stacks Project Authors, n.d., [Tag 08G8](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/08G8)); it does not refute the fixed-interval stalkwise criterion on the page.

An infinite direct sum of contractible two-term free complexes placed in disjoint, successively negative degrees represents the zero, hence perfect, derived object, yet its identity has no finite degreewise alternating sum on that unbounded representative. Thus the literal representative-based formula needs local bounded representatives or another specified interpretation; this is a conditional scope objection, not a reason to restore the deletion or deny the intrinsic trace of the perfect object.

context/same_cote_33/MPL_33_098-146_note.text: The assertion that the normalization of a one-dimensional local domain is a semilocal PID is correct under the usual Noetherian convention: normalization is semilocal Dedekind, and its invertible ideals are principal (The Stacks Project Authors, n.d., [Tags 09IG](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/09IG), [09N2](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/09N2), [02M9](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/02M9)). context/same_cote_33/MPL_33_098-146_note.section: ### N54. The literal étale criterion admits a dual-number counterexample
context/same_cote_33/MPL_33_098-146_note.text: In condition (c), finite separability of $\kappa(y)/\kappa(x)$ alone does not imply the subsequent equality $m_y=m_xO_y$: $\operatorname{Spec}(k[\varepsilon]/\varepsilon^2)\to\operatorname{Spec}k$ is finite, flat and finitely presented, with residue extension $k/k$, but has $m_y=(\varepsilon)\ne0$. Its nonreduced fibre prevents étaleness, in agreement with the criterion requiring étale fibres (The Stacks Project Authors, n.d., [Tag 03PC](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/03PC), Proposition 59.26.2). This is a counterexample to the isolated residue-field-only wording as transcribed, not to the stronger condition printed immediately afterward or to an unseen theorem elsewhere.

Thus the literal representative-based formula needs local bounded representatives or another specified interpretation; this is a conditional scope objection, not a reason to restore the deletion or deny the intrinsic trace of the perfect object.

The primary complete-local theorem explicitly assumes completeness (The Stacks Project Authors, n.d., [Tag 0C0S](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/0C0S)). This is a conditional counterexample to the isolated wording, and the right next step is to recover earlier conventions from the reused source before declaring its full theorem false.

This is our second conditional scope test, distinct from N50, not an assertion that the unseen preceding hypotheses were absent.

context/same_cote_33/MPL_33_098-146_note.section: ### N09. The noetherian expectation for relative direct image
context/same_cote_33/MPL_33_098-146_note.text: “C'est peut-être vrai dès que $Y$ est noethérien” concerns finite **relative** cohomological dimension of $f_*$, in the surrounding finite-type discussion, rather than finite absolute cohomological dimension of $Y$. The finite-type-over-a-field case has a direct modern counterpart (The Stacks Project Authors, n.d., [Tag 0F10](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/0F10)), and Illusie (2014, Exposé XVIII_A, Corollary 1.4) proves the relative $\ell$-torsion statement for finite-dimensional noetherian $Y$ with $\ell$ invertible on $Y$. Those results confirm qualified versions; these notes leave the draft's full “merely noetherian” scope unresolved and do not offer the absolute cohomology of a field as a counterexample to it.

context/same_cote_33/MPL_33_098-146_note.section: ### N20. Curves, singular coefficients and rationality of L-functions
context/same_cote_33/MPL_33_098-146_note.text: “Il semble que pour les courbes, on récupère … (sans résolution des singularités) … $\rightsquigarrow$ rationalité des fonctions $L$” is a proposed application of the formalism, not a proved curve theorem on this page. A proof would have to identify the extension-by-zero or immersion argument, justify the local terms for the singular coefficient sheaf, and then pass from the trace identities to the Euler product/determinant identity. The finished SGA 5 provides distinct comparison destinations for Lefschetz and for rationality, but the present evidence does not identify this draft with a particular circulated version (Grothendieck, 1977, Exposé III; Illusie, 1977, volume contents).

context/same_cote_33/MPL_33_098-146_note.section: ### N22. Fixed points require local multiplicities
context/same_cote_33/MPL_33_098-146_note.text: The schematic equality with “nb de pts fixes” is immediately qualified by “avec grain de sel,” and isolated fixed points are said to require suitable multiplicities. The later promise “On donnera l'approche de Verdier” leaves both the general coefficient-sheaf construction and the promised elementary derivation to be developed beyond this opening paragraph. This adds a trace/local-term programme, not a count of fixed points with multiplicity one; comparison with the finished exposition belongs at Grothendieck (1977, Exposé III, §§3–4).

context/same_cote_33/MPL_33_098-146_note.section: ### N34. Degree-zero correspondences and an omitted H-zero
context/same_cote_33/MPL_33_098-146_note.text: The first display equates $\operatorname{Hom}^0$ with an entire $R\Gamma R\mathcal Hom$ expression, although the surrounding chain is explicitly about “correspondances cohomologiques de degré $0$.” The natural type-correct interpretation would take $H^0$ of the latter complex, but no such $H^0$ has been supplied in the transcription. Grothendieck (1977, Exposé III, §§2–3) is a comparison destination for the derived functoriality and correspondence construction, not evidence that the missing characters were present on this sheet.

context/same_cote_33/MPL_33_098-146_note.section: ### N36. A local pairing is cancelled, then the construction restarts
context/same_cote_33/MPL_33_098-146_note.text: The paragraph beginning “Cet accouplement est induit par un accouplement de nature locale” is cancelled on 144, including the doubtful parenthesis “[pas besoin] que $f$ et $g$ soient propres.” Scan 146 restarts with a trace map and cyclic pairings for pseudo-coherent finite-Tor-dimensional complexes, but the two pages do not finish the entire local-to-global Lefschetz–Verdier theorem. This adds evidence of a change in exposition and should not be recorded as a proved rejection of local pairings or as a completed theorem without properness (compare Grothendieck, 1977, Exposé III, §4).

context/same_cote_33/MPL_33_098-146_note.text: The progression from pseudo-coherence and Tor dimension to contraction, then to a sheaf-level trace, is closely aligned with the later organization of perfect-complex theory. context/same_cote_33/MPL_33_002-049_note.section: ### N33. Connected scheme fibres do not alone force a trace isomorphism
context/same_cote_33/MPL_33_002-049_note.text: If “fibres conn. non vides” means ordinary scheme-theoretic connectedness, $\operatorname{Spec}\mathbb C\to\operatorname{Spec}\mathbb R$ is a smooth finite étale map of relative dimension zero with connected nonempty fibre, but its geometric fibre has two points. For $A=\mathbb F_3$, the trace on that geometric stalk is the sum $A^2\to A$, not an isomorphism, by the finite étale trace description in [Stacks 03SH](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/03SH). The explicit “géom. connexe” on 028 makes it especially useful to check whether 034 uses a convention about geometric fibres or omits a qualification.

context/same_cote_33/MPL_33_098-146_note.section: ### N10. A point already exhibits infinite Tor
context/same_cote_33/MPL_33_098-146_note.text: A concrete check of “même si $X$ … un pt géométrique” is $A=\mathbb Z/\ell^2\mathbb Z$ and $M=A/\ell A$: the resolution with every differential multiplication by $\ell$ is exact, while tensoring it with $M$ makes every differential zero. Hence $\operatorname{Tor}_i^A(M,M)\cong M$ for every $i\geq0$, so locally constant finite modules do not automatically give bounded derived tensor products. This is our elementary example, adding an explicit witness to the manuscript's warning, not a claim that the example is written there.

context/same_cote_33/MPL_33_098-146_note.section: ### N34. Degree-zero correspondences and an omitted H-zero
context/same_cote_33/MPL_33_098-146_note.text: The first display equates $\operatorname{Hom}^0$ with an entire $R\Gamma R\mathcal Hom$ expression, although the surrounding chain is explicitly about “correspondances cohomologiques de degré $0$.” The natural type-correct interpretation would take $H^0$ of the latter complex, but no such $H^0$ has been supplied in the transcription. Grothendieck (1977, Exposé III, §§2–3) is a comparison destination for the derived functoriality and correspondence construction, not evidence that the missing characters were present on this sheet.

context/same_cote_33/MPL_33_098-146_note.section: ### N37. The local trace and the symmetry sign
context/same_cote_33/MPL_33_098-146_note.text: The trace diagram and the final equality with “$\operatorname{sym}$” encode cyclicity through the symmetry of the derived tensor category, so the sign rule is part of the construction and not optional decoration. A proof can use local strictly perfect representatives and then check descent and compatibility of evaluation/coevaluation; the ringed-site duality formulation provides this framework (The Stacks Project Authors, n.d., [Tag 0FPP](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/0FPP)). The displayed supertrace and the two composition expressions are written here, but the page stops before a full verification of their compatibility.

context/same_cote_33/MPL_33_098-146_note.section: ### N54. The literal étale criterion admits a dual-number counterexample
context/same_cote_33/MPL_33_098-146_note.text: In condition (c), finite separability of $\kappa(y)/\kappa(x)$ alone does not imply the subsequent equality $m_y=m_xO_y$: $\operatorname{Spec}(k[\varepsilon]/\varepsilon^2)\to\operatorname{Spec}k$ is finite, flat and finitely presented, with residue extension $k/k$, but has $m_y=(\varepsilon)\ne0$. Its nonreduced fibre prevents étaleness, in agreement with the criterion requiring étale fibres (The Stacks Project Authors, n.d., [Tag 03PC](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/03PC), Proposition 59.26.2). This is a counterexample to the isolated residue-field-only wording as transcribed, not to the stronger condition printed immediately afterward or to an unseen theorem elsewhere.
